name: Talong
sunlight: Full sun, 6 or more hours a day
sourceNote: Temperature, rainfall, pH, soil and crop-cycle ranges are from FAO EcoCrop datasheet 1965 (Solanum melongena). Care steps are general garden guidance.
careTips: Plant in soft garden soil that drains well. Eggplant dislikes soggy roots.
Keep plants 50–60 cm apart so the roots do not compete for food.
Stake each plant. Branches heavy with fruit snap easily in wind.
Water at the base and avoid wetting the leaves, which helps stop leaf disease.
Mulch with dry grass or rice straw to keep moisture in and weeds down.
pestTips: Tiny holes in young leaves usually mean flea beetles. Cover seedlings with a light net until they are bigger.
Mix a few drops of dish soap in a spray bottle of water and spray under the leaves in the evening.
Remove old yellow leaves at the bottom so air can move and bugs have fewer places to hide.

tasks.detail: Start seeds in a tray or small pots. Keep them moist and move the seedlings to the bed when they have 4–5 leaves (about 3–4 weeks).
Water lightly every morning. The soil should feel damp, not soggy.
Mix a handful of compost or aged manure into the soil around each seedling.
tasks.extra: Keep it away from the stem.

tasks.detail: Tie each plant loosely to a stake. Cut off old yellow leaves at the bottom so air can flow.
tiny holes in the leaves (flea beetles) or curled, sticky leaves
tasks.extra: spray soapy water or neem oil under the leaves in the evening.

tasks.detail: Add another handful of compost around each plant when the first flowers appear.
the fruits are shiny and firm, and the skin springs back when pressed lightly
tasks.extra: Cut with scissors and leave a short piece of stem. Pick often so the plant keeps producing.

name: Ampalaya
spacing: About 60–90 cm apart, with a trellis
sourceNote: Typical growing ranges from agricultural extension guidance. Not yet checked against the FAO EcoCrop datasheet. Look the crop up at gaez.fao.org/pages/ecocrop-search before relying on exact numbers. FAO EcoCrop entry 7795 says flowers appear 30–35 days after planting and fruit can be picked after 50–70 days.
careTips: Grows best in well-drained soft or sandy-loam soil rich in compost.
Build a bamboo trellis early. Ampalaya is a weak climber and needs support.
Pick fruits young, every 2–3 days. They mature fast and turn orange-red.
pestTips: Wrap young fruits in old newspaper or paper bags to stop fruit flies from stinging them.
Spray aphids off with a gentle stream of water or soapy water.

tasks.detail: Soak the seeds in water overnight first, then plant 2–3 seeds per hole.
Keep the soil damp but not muddy.
Mix compost into the soil around the seedlings.
Set up a bamboo trellis and guide the vines up it every few days.
fruit fly stings on young fruit, or white powder on the leaves
tasks.extra: wrap young fruits in paper bags and spray soapy water on the leaves.

tasks.detail: Water deeply while the fruits are growing.
the fruits are green, bumpy and about 15–20 cm long, before they turn yellow-orange
tasks.extra: Pick every 2–3 days with scissors because the fruits mature fast.

name: Sitao
spacing: About 30 cm apart, on a trellis
sourceNote: Typical growing ranges from agricultural extension guidance. Not yet checked against the FAO EcoCrop datasheet. Look the crop up at gaez.fao.org/pages/ecocrop-search before relying on exact numbers.
careTips: Sow seeds straight into the bed. Yardlong beans dislike being moved.
Thin to the 2 strongest plants per hole so they have room.
Beans make some of their own plant food, so go easy on fertiliser.
Give the vines a trellis or sticks to climb.
pestTips: Tiny black or green bugs (aphids) on young shoots: spray them off with water or soapy water.
Pick pods often. Old pods left on the vine slow down new ones.

tasks.detail: Plant 2–3 seeds per hole, about 30 cm apart.
Keep the soil lightly damp until the seedlings are up.
Thin to the strongest 2 plants per hole and push in a stick or trellis for the vines.
Add a light layer of compost. Do not over-feed, since too much food gives leaves but few pods.
tiny black or green bugs (aphids) clustered on young shoots
tasks.extra: spray them off with water or soapy water.

tasks.detail: Water well when the flowers appear so the pods set.
the pods are slim, long and snap easily, before the seeds make them bulge
tasks.extra: Pick every 2 days to keep new pods coming.

name: Kangkong
sourceNote: Typical growing ranges from agricultural extension guidance. Not yet checked against the FAO EcoCrop datasheet. Look the crop up at gaez.fao.org/pages/ecocrop-search before relying on exact numbers.
careTips: Loves wet, muddy soil. Keep the bed moist all the time.
Cut stems 5 cm above the soil so new leaves regrow again and again.
Sandy soil dries too fast. Use a raised bed with compost instead.
pestTips: Check leaves every morning for caterpillars and pick them off by hand.
If many leaf-eaters appear, spray soapy water in the evening.

tasks.detail: Plant seeds or 15 cm stem cuttings in wet soil.
Keep the soil wet at all times.
Add compost or a little manure. Leafy crops love extra nitrogen.
caterpillars or holes in the leaves
tasks.extra: pick them off by hand in the morning.

tasks.detail: Pinch off the growing tips so the plant becomes bushy.
the stems are about 25–30 cm long
tasks.extra: Cut 5 cm above the soil. It regrows for another harvest in 2–3 weeks.

name: Kamatis
sunlight: Full sun, 6 or more hours a day
sourceNote: Typical growing ranges from agricultural extension guidance. Not yet checked against the FAO EcoCrop datasheet. Look the crop up at gaez.fao.org/pages/ecocrop-search before relying on exact numbers.
careTips: Loves soft, nutrient-rich soil and full sun.
Water at the base, not on the leaves.
Keep watering steady. Swings between dry and soaked can crack the fruit.

pestTips: Tiny white flying bugs (whiteflies) under the leaves: spray mild soapy water or dust a little wood ash.
Remove badly damaged leaves and throw them away instead of composting them.

tasks.detail: Start seeds in a tray and move the seedlings to the bed after about 4 weeks.

Mix compost into the soil around each seedling.
Pinch off small side shoots between the main stem and branches, and tie the main stem to a stake.
tiny white flying bugs (whiteflies) or curled leaves
tasks.extra: spray mild soapy water under the leaves or dust a little wood ash.

tasks.detail: Water at the base and keep it even. Do not let the soil swing between dry and soaked.
the fruits are fully red, or just starting to blush pink
tasks.extra: Twist or cut the fruit off with its stem. Pick every 2–3 days.

Spray soapy water if leaf-eating bugs appear.

tasks.detail: Soak the seeds overnight, then plant 2–3 seeds per hole.
Keep the soil lightly damp until the seedlings are up.
Mix compost around the base of each plant.
Cut off the lowest yellow leaves so air can move through the plant.
egg clusters or leaf-eating bugs under the leaves
tasks.extra: wipe clusters off with a damp cloth and spray soapy water.

tasks.detail: Water deeply once a week if there has been no rain.
the pods are 7–10 cm long and still soft
tasks.extra: Pick every day or two, and wear gloves.

name: Pechay

holes in the leaves or tiny black beetles

tasks.detail: the plants are 15–20 cm tall with firm, bright green leaves
tasks.extra: Pull up the whole plant or cut it at the base in the morning.

tasks.detail: Sow seeds thinly and cover lightly with fine soil.

Mix a thin layer of compost into the soil around the plants.

tasks.extra: wash them off with water or spray soapy water.

Mix a thin layer of compost into the soil around the plants.
chewed leaves or small caterpillars
